statement: The same batch judgment text is stored under many judgment_ids, and v2 gives every copy the batch's last printed disposition. Rows for petitions that were decided differently carry a wrong outcome, and the holdout counts such a batch once.
evidence: 62 text blobs are shared by 292 of the 3,936 judgment_ids (OUTCOMES_V2.csv text_source). J&K batch of 03.11.2025 (holdout H042): 34 rows 'dismissed', 10 abstain, 1 allowed. The rows for WP(C) 1319/2024 and 1708/2024 (ground truth allowed), 1653/2024 (partly allowed) and 2301/2024 (AFT order set aside) all say 'dismissed' with the p.260 excerpt of a different petition. Other groups: 24 Delhi rows disposed_of_with_directions, 18 Delhi rows partly_allowed, 17 Delhi rows disposed_of_with_directions.
requested_action: Join OUTCOMES_V2 to the identity register's same-text groups. Set every row in a same-text group, and every row whose proceeding names several case numbers, to OUTCOME_UNVERIFIED until per-proceeding splitting exists. Report coverage and label counts per distinct text as well as per judgment_id.

statement: The holdout is single-coded, not double-coded. Reviewer A covers H001-H028 and reviewer B covers H029-H056 with no overlap, so there is no inter-reviewer agreement figure and no second reading of any outcome.
evidence: ground_truth_A.csv has 28 holdout ids, ground_truth_B.csv has 28, intersection 0. The two reviewers also used different conventions: A coded substance where the court printed only 'disposed of' (H021 allowed, H024 allowed, H026 dismissed_as_withdrawn, H027 set_aside_and_remanded); B coded the printed words in the same situation (H034 disposed_of_with_directions although relief was granted).
requested_action: Say 'one blind reviewer per judgment' in HOLDOUT_EVALUATION.md. Have the other reviewer blind-code at least the 7 errors, the 11 abstentions and 10 further rows. Write the labelling convention (printed words or substance) down before the next holdout.

statement: The 84.1% headline is unweighted over a sample that over-represents the Supreme Court and under-represents Delhi. Weighted to the population the sample was drawn from, precision is about 79%.
evidence: Eligible population 3,862 judgments: Delhi 1,628 (42%), P&H 1,201, J&K 403, SC 321 (8%), Allahabad 309. Sample: SC 20 of 56 (36%), Delhi 8 (14%). Post-stratified by court x stratum: precision 78.9%, coverage 87.1% (cells hold 2 to 8 judgments, so this is indicative only). Delhi is 4/7 in the sample.
requested_action: Report the weighted figure beside the unweighted one and stop calling the sample representative without that qualification. Draw the next holdout proportionally, or large enough per court to weight.

statement: The baseline comparison is biased against the crawler and the Cycle 10 extractor because it requires an exact label match, and their vocabularies have no 'disposed_of_with_directions' or 'transferred'.
evidence: eval_holdout_c11.py baseline(): `vals == scorable`. Crawler 'disposed' can never equal ground truth 'disposed_of_with_directions' or 'transferred'. Compared by outcome family (allowed / partly_allowed / dismissed / disposed): crawler 33/44 = 75.0% (reported 28/44 = 63.6%), Cycle 10 extractor 31/48 = 64.6% (reported 25/48 = 52.1%), v2 38/44 = 86.4%. Two-sided 95% intervals overlap (v2 73-94%, crawler 61-85%).
requested_action: Report family-level baselines. Replace 'substantially better than both baselines' with the measured margins and intervals.

statement: 'Partly succeeds' is read as allowed, and one extent-qualified allowance was not abstained although the README says it should be.
evidence: H011: 'The appeal partly succeeds in the above terms' -> allowed (v2core _INTRANS_RE has no 'partly' handling). Corpus: J-123f221f41ed354a 'To the aforesaid extent ... this petition is allowed' -> allowed.
requested_action: Fix in v3 and add both sentences as tests. No change to v1.0.0 outputs, which stay AUTOMATED_CANDIDATE_NOT_VERIFIED.

statement: Proposition recall against the blind ground-truth holdings is low: about 1 in 8 reviewer-identified holdings appears among v2 court candidates.
evidence: 133 distinct ground-truth holdings in 52 holdout judgments; 130 are locatable in the text layer. Matched to a COURT_HOLDING or COURT_REASONING candidate on the same page (+/-1) with at least 40 characters of common text: 16/133 = 12.0% (Wilson 95% 7.5% to 18.6%). Matched to a candidate of any origin: 50/133 = 37.6%; 29 of the 34 extra matches are labelled OTHER_OR_UNCERTAIN. Only 14 of 52 judgments have any holding matched. Court voice is detected from a fixed phrase list ('we hold', 'in our view', ...), and most holdings are plain declarative sentences.
requested_action: State the recall figure in the README. Do not use PROPOSITIONS_V2 as a holdings index or as a negative ('no holding on X found'). Treat it as a list of leads only.

statement: Origin labels are not precise enough to filter on. Court-voice labels are right about 9 times in 10; QUOTED_PRECEDENT and LOWER_COURT_FINDING are confused with each other and with other quoted material.
evidence: Sample of 100 outside dev and holdout: COURT_HOLDING_CANDIDATE 37/40 (92.5%, Wilson 80.1-97.4); COURT_REASONING_CANDIDATE 17/20 (85.0%, 64.0-94.8); QUOTED_PRECEDENT 11/15 (73.3%, 48.0-89.1); PARTY_SUBMISSION 8/10 (80.0%, 49.0-94.3); EDITORIAL_HEADNOTE 10/10 (100%, 72.2-100); LOWER_COURT_FINDING 3/5 (60.0%, 23.1-88.2). Wrong court labels: CHC02 and CHC20 and CRC12 are inside quotations, CRC10 is headnote text, CRC16 is a party statement, CHC26 is a cover block. attributed_to was wrong or garbled in 4 of the 5 QUOTED_PRECEDENT rows that had one.
requested_action: Keep every proposition NOT_VERIFIED_NOT_A_HOLDING. Do not surface attributed_to to users. Fix quote-span tracking (F08) before re-measuring.

statement: A court's own operative sentence that follows a closing quotation mark can be treated as quoted. This mislabels propositions and causes outcome abstentions.
evidence: QP14 (hc-ph-2012-crwp-221-2000): 'Accordingly, Registry is directed to send paper book of this case to the Armed Forces Tribunal' labelled QUOTED_PRECEDENT attributed to 'Section 34'; that judgment's outcome is OUTCOME_UNVERIFIED. Holdout H034 and H055 abstain with ONLY_QUOTED_DISPOSITION_LANGUAGE_FOUND although the disposing sentence is the court's own, after the quote closes. 51 corpus rows carry that abstain reason.
requested_action: Review the 51 ONLY_QUOTED_DISPOSITION_LANGUAGE_FOUND rows by hand first; fix quote closing in v3.

statement: The blinding and freeze claims cannot be verified from the artifacts. I found no sign of leakage.
evidence: Ground truth files date from 02:21-02:23; v2core.py and extract_v2.py were last modified at 05:04 and 05:11; predictions were written at 05:18; all arrive in one commit (b6340e20). The scorer was changed twice after results were seen (disclosed in the report). No holdout id, sha or doc_id appears in tools, tests or dev_gold.json; re-running the 56 ids gives a byte-identical OUTCOMES_V2.csv.
requested_action: Next time commit the frozen tool hashes and the scorer before the ground truth is unsealed, in separate commits.

statement: Proceeding labels are unreliable and the scorer does not test them when all proceedings were decided alike.
evidence: H013: two appeals dismissed, v2 has a row for one only. H008: row names one of two appeals and its excerpt is the lead-in 'We accordingly dispose of the appeals as under :'. Labels carry stray text ('TIA v. UNION OF INDIA & ORS. (Civil Appeal 1536 of', 'DELHI AT NEW DELHI W.P.(C) ...') and cited-case numbers as if they were host numbers (Civil Appeal 418-2012 in DC03 and DC18; Civil Appeal 5605 of 2010 in DO08). 1,374 non-abstained rows name three or more case numbers.
requested_action: Do not use the proceeding column to attach outcomes to case numbers. Add a proceeding-level completeness measure to the next evaluation.

statement: Some abstain reasons do not describe what is in the text, and some excerpts carry page furniture.
evidence: H024 ONLY_MISC_APPLICATION_DISPOSAL_FOUND (the order has no misc-application disposal); H014 NO_DISPOSITION_IN_OPERATIVE_PART (text prints 'Appeals are allowed to the above extent', the README's extent-qualified case). 6,543 of 51,250 proposition spans cross a page marker; outcome excerpts DC09 and DC20 include a signature stamp and running header mid-sentence. For 12 not_final rows the excerpt is the tail of the char_start-char_end span, not its start.
requested_action: Cosmetic for now; fix with v3. Reviewers should not triage on abstain_reason alone.

statement: The strict figure is right and the scoring rules are applied as written. The verdict (below the 95% bar) stands under every reading.
evidence: Independent re-score: 37 correct, 7 incorrect, 11 abstained, 1 not scorable; 37/44 = 84.1%, one-sided 95% lower bound 73.1%, two-sided 70.6% to 92.1%. On printed-words convention 40/44 = 90.9% (78.8% to 96.4%). All 7 errors confirmed against source (4 are extractor errors on any convention, 3 depend on the convention). 10 sampled CORRECT rows confirmed 10/10. All 11 abstentions are real abstentions. In 6 of them (H002, H006, H014, H034, H047, H055) the text layer prints a plain disposing sentence, so they cost coverage, not precision.

statement: Beyond the holdout, v2's reading of the printed disposition was right in all 30 sampled crawler-versus-old-extractor disagreements.
evidence: 20/20 where v2 sides with the crawler and 10/10 where it sides with the old extractor (Wilson lower bound 88.6% pooled). 18 of the 20 crawler-side rows are P&H orders, most on one template ('the writ petition is accordingly dismissed ... Pending application(s), if any, stands disposed of'), so this mostly confirms that one pattern. DO06 prints 'allowed' with restricted relief; the crawler's partly_allowed is defensible on substance.
